main_body: Round stone tower with a conical green tiled roof, a small framed window with flower box, and an arched wooden door on a stone plinth
top_band: Green scalloped conical roof, rows ~3-39, light-to-dark green tile courses, with a brown rim and dark green eave line at rows 39-41
evidence: Reading the centre column: gold finial (rows 0-3), then a large green tiled roof slope (rows 4-38) that reads as a surface seen from above. Below it is a brown rim with a dark green eave shadow (rows 39-41), then the stone front face (rows 42-93) with a framed window and sill and a door inset in a stone surround. The roof slope is a real, large top surface and the wall is a separate south face, so it reads as a 3/4 building rather than a flat elevation. The conical roof is a fairly frontal triangle, but the tile courses and overhanging eave carry the slope.

style.evidence: The roof has about 5 green steps with per-tile scallops and highlights. The stone wall has light, mid and dark greys with brick mortar lines. Outlines are dark green next to the roof and dark purple-grey next to the stone, so they are tinted rather than black. The window glass, flower box and door planks add detail. Individual bricks are fairly smooth, with little speckle compared with the references' plaster and shingle grain, so density is a little lower, but the piece would sit acceptably next to them.
